en.title: Laravel Development
en.description:
Laravel is our primary backend framework — most of what we build runs on it. We design and develop custom web applications, REST and GraphQL APIs, admin panels and multi-tenant SaaS products: from architecture and database design to queues, scheduling, caching, billing and third-party integrations.

What we build with Laravel

  • SaaS platforms and subscription products — our own DigiPulse marketing platform is a Laravel application with multi-channel publishing, scheduling and analytics.
  • REST APIs for mobile and SPA frontends — VetSpace's backend is a Laravel API serving a Nuxt frontend and mobile clients, with GraphQL where the data model calls for it.
  • Custom admin panels and content tools — this very website runs on a Laravel CMS we built, with Filament for the admin UI.
  • E-commerce backends, booking systems and internal business tools that don't fit off-the-shelf software.

How we work

We follow Laravel conventions instead of fighting them: Eloquent where it helps, the query builder where it's faster, queues for anything heavy, events and listeners to keep controllers thin. Code is covered by PHPUnit tests, formatted with Pint and reviewed before merge — so the codebase stays easy to extend and cheap to support years later.

Existing Laravel codebase? We take those too

A large part of our work is inheriting projects built by other teams. We start with an audit — dependencies, test coverage, N+1 queries, security issues — then stabilize, refactor and extend without breaking production. If your Laravel app is slow, fragile or abandoned by its developers, that's exactly the kind of work we do.

Tell us about your project — we'll give you an honest assessment of scope, stack and timeline.

Under the hood

A typical Laravel feature from our codebase — a queued job that publishes a scheduled post in DigiPulse, with retries and backoff handled by the framework:

class PublishScheduledPost implements ShouldQueue
{
    use Dispatchable, InteractsWithQueue, Queueable, SerializesModels;

    public int $tries = 3;
    public array $backoff = [30, 120, 600];

    public function __construct(public readonly ScheduledPost $post) {}

    public function handle(ChannelPublisher $publisher): void
    {
        $result = $publisher->publish($this->post);

        $this->post->update([
            'status'       => PostStatus::Published,
            'published_at' => now(),
            'external_id'  => $result->id,
        ]);
    }
}

Queued job with exponential backoff — heavy work never blocks the request cycle.

en.title: Symfony Development
en.description:
Symfony is our choice for projects that need enterprise-grade structure: strict architecture, long-term maintainability and components that integrate cleanly with the rest of the PHP ecosystem. We use it for complex backends, API-first applications and systems where the domain model is too rich for a lighter framework.

Where Symfony fits best

  • API-first backends built on API Platform or hand-rolled REST/GraphQL endpoints with clean serialization and versioning.
  • Complex business systems — invoicing, logistics, multi-organization platforms — where Symfony's form, validator and workflow components pay for themselves.
  • Long-lived enterprise codebases where Symfony's LTS releases and predictable upgrade path matter more than the newest features.
  • Microservices and standalone components — many Symfony components (Console, HttpClient, Messenger, EventDispatcher) work perfectly inside non-Symfony projects too.

Our approach

We structure Symfony applications around the domain, not around the framework: thin controllers, explicit services, Doctrine entities kept honest, business logic testable without booting the kernel. Messenger for async work, proper dependency injection, configuration as code — the result is a codebase a new developer can navigate in a day.

Migration and modernization

If you have a legacy PHP application — Zend, Symfony 2/3/4, or framework-less spaghetti — we can migrate it incrementally to a modern Symfony version. We run old and new code side by side, move module by module, and keep the business running throughout. No big-bang rewrites that take a year and deliver nothing.

Share your requirements — we'll tell you honestly whether Symfony, Laravel or something else fits better.

Under the hood

Async work in Symfony goes through Messenger — a command, a handler, and transport config. Nothing magic, everything explicit:

#[AsMessageHandler]
final class GenerateInvoiceHandler
{
    public function __construct(
        private InvoiceRepository $invoices,
        private PdfRenderer $pdf,
    ) {}

    public function __invoke(GenerateInvoice $command): void
    {
        $invoice = $this->invoices->get($command->invoiceId);
        $this->pdf->render($invoice);
        $invoice->markGenerated();
    }
}

And the request lifecycle stays predictable — the framework handles routing, validation and serialization, your code handles the domain:

Request → Router → Controller → DTO + Validator → Handler → Doctrine → Response
                      │
                      └─► Messenger ──► async worker (Doctrine transport / RabbitMQ)

en.title: Golang Development
en.description:
We use Go where PHP stops being the right tool: high-throughput services, background workers, network-intensive processing and software that needs to run lean on a server. Go's concurrency model and single-binary deployment make it ideal for the unglamorous infrastructure work that keeps products fast.

What we build in Go

  • AI-processing microservices — NetPostPanel, our AI content platform, runs its provider orchestration, RAG pipeline and semantic filtering as Go services that handle concurrent LLM calls efficiently.
  • Scrapers and data pipelines — concurrent crawlers that fetch, parse and normalize content at rates PHP workers can't match.
  • Internal APIs and webhooks — small, fast services that sit next to a Laravel monolith and take the load it shouldn't carry.
  • CLI tools and automation — deployment helpers, importers and maintenance utilities that compile to one binary and run anywhere.

Go alongside PHP, not instead of it

Our typical architecture is a Laravel application doing what Laravel does well — HTTP, auth, admin, billing — with Go services behind it doing what Go does well: fan-out concurrency, streaming, CPU-heavy processing. They talk over HTTP, queues and webhooks. You get the productivity of PHP where it matters and the performance of Go where it matters.

How we deliver

Go code we write is intentionally boring: standard library first, minimal dependencies, structured logging, graceful shutdown, Dockerfile included. If it runs on our Linux servers today, it'll run on yours — and the next developer won't need to reverse-engineer clever tricks.

If you have a PHP bottleneck that keeps growing, or a service that should exist outside the monolith — that's a good reason to talk.

Under the hood

Fan-out in Go is a dozen lines, not a framework — this is the pattern behind NetPostPanel's concurrent provider calls:

func fetchAll(ctx context.Context, urls []string) []Result {
    results := make(chan Result, len(urls))
    var wg sync.WaitGroup

    for _, u := range urls {
        wg.Add(1)
        go func(url string) {
            defer wg.Done()
            results <- fetch(ctx, url)
        }(u)
    }

    wg.Wait()
    close(results)
    return slices.Collect(results)
}

And where it sits in the bigger picture:

Browser ──► Laravel app ──► HTTP ──► Go service ──► LLM provider × N (concurrent)
                │                        │
                └─► MySQL                └─► RAG: embed → vector search → rerank

en.title: Responsive Web Applications

We build web applications that work flawlessly on every screen — phones, tablets, desktops. Mobile-first layouts, touch-friendly UI, fast load times and accessible markup as standard, not an afterthought.

From a marketing site to a complex web app, we ensure consistent behavior across browsers and devices: responsive grids, adaptive images, offline-tolerant forms and Core Web Vitals optimization.

What Are Responsive Web Apps

It can be truly upsetting when you try to get access to a web app and fail due to its incompatibility with your device. Besides, today users mostly prefer to use mobile devices for their working, entertainment, or shopping experiences. And a diverse range of these devices often becomes a pitfall for businesses that offer their apps to customers. 
That all can be mitigated by using responsive web apps, which have no limits for accessing them from all types of devices regardless of their model, brand, OS types, screen dimensions, etc. 

Our team has provided responsive web app development services for businesses for several years already. 

Where Can Responsive Web Apps Come in Handy

By making your web app mobile responsive, you can achieve multiple goals:

  • Provide your employees with an opportunity to use a single app from all devices while performing their working routines.
  • Enhance your clientele by offering it an opportunity to get access to your products/services through an app from all devices.

As these goals are commonly relevant, you can use mobile-responsive web apps for the following ideas:

  • Effective corporate app development.
  • E-commerce platform development.
  • Game development for multiple platforms.
  • Service apps for customers' access.

And that is just the tip of the iceberg, as responsive web apps can be used almost everywhere!

Top-Notch Responsive App Development Services by DigiSpace

In our company, you can get high-class web development services, which also include responsive app development and maintenance. We use new-gen technologies and implement Bootstrap responsive web development methods to gain results which will please even the most sophisticated user. Our skills and readiness for non-standard tasks are at your service in DigiSpace!

Responsive in practice

Modern responsive layout is a few lines of CSS — fluid type and a grid that adapts without breakpoints:

.cards {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr));
  gap: clamp(16px, 3vw, 32px);
}

h1 { font-size: clamp(1.75rem, 1.2rem + 2.5vw, 3rem); }

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  * { animation: none; transition: none; }
}

Fluid sizing with clamp(), intrinsic grids, reduced-motion respect — responsive means more than "fits on a phone".

WordPress powers a third of the web for a reason: for content sites, marketing pages and small-to-medium e-commerce it's still the fastest way from idea to launch. We build WordPress sites that are fast, secure and actually maintainable — not the usual pile of forty plugins held together by hope.

What we do with WordPress

  • Corporate and marketing websites — our DigiSpace Studio project is a WordPress-based studio for clients who need a professional site quickly and on a sane budget.
  • Custom themes built on your design, not a bought template with your logo pasted in. Clean HTML, proper asset loading, no page-builder bloat.

  • WooCommerce stores — product catalogues, checkout customization, payment and shipping integrations.
  • Migrations and rescues — moving sites between hosts, fixing hacked or broken installs, updating sites nobody dared touch for years.

Fast and safe by default

A WordPress site's reputation problems — slowness and hacks — come from poor setup, not from WordPress itself. We configure proper caching, image optimization, a minimal plugin set with known maintenance status, security hardening and automated backups. The result scores well on Core Web Vitals and doesn't keep you up at night.

When WordPress is not the answer

We build custom Laravel applications too, and we'll tell you honestly when your project has outgrown WordPress — complex business logic, heavy integrations, multi-system workflows. If WordPress fits, we'll build it well. If it doesn't, we'll say so.

WordPress done properly

Custom functionality goes into a plugin or the theme's hooks — never into a page builder blob:

add_action('rest_api_init', function () {
    register_rest_route('studio/v1', '/portfolio', [
        'methods'  => 'GET',
        'callback' => fn() => get_posts([
            'post_type'   => 'portfolio',
            'numberposts' => 12,
        ]),
        'permission_callback' => '__return_true',
    ]);
});

And the anatomy of a healthy WordPress install:

Browser ──► Nginx ──► PHP-FPM ──► WordPress
                              ├─► theme (custom, no builder)
                              ├─► plugins (minimal, maintained)
                              └─► MySQL ──► object cache (Redis)

Проблеми репутації WordPress — повільність і злами — йдуть від поганого налаштування, а не від самого WordPress. pl.description:

Co robimy na WordPress

  • Strony korporacyjne i marketingowe — nasz projekt DigiSpace Studio to studio oparte na WordPress dla klientów, którzy potrzebują profesjonalnej strony szybko i w rozsądnym budżecie.
  • Dedykowane motywy na podstawie Twojego projektu, a nie kupiony szablon z wklejonym logo. Czysty HTML, prawidłowe ładowanie zasobów, żadnego balastu page-buildera.
  • Dedykowane wtyczki i integracje — gdy istniejące wtyczki nie robią tego, czego potrzebujesz, piszemy brakujący element zamiast instalować kolejne trzy.
  • Sklepy WooCommerce — katalogi produktów, dostosowanie checkoutu, integracje płatności i dostawy.
  • Migracje i ratowanie — przenoszenie stron między hostingami, naprawa zhakowanych lub popsutych instalacji, aktualizacja stron, których nikt nie odważył się dotknąć latami.

Szybko i bezpiecznie domyślnie

Problemy reputacji WordPressa — wolność i włamania — wynikają ze złej konfiguracji, a nie z samego WordPressa. Konfigurujemy prawidłowe cache'owanie, optymalizację obrazów, minimalny zestaw wtyczek o znanym stanie wsparcia, hardening bezpieczeństwa i automatyczne kopie zapasowe. Efekt dobrze wypada w Core Web Vitals i nie zabiera snu.

Kiedy WordPress nie jest odpowiedzią

Budujemy też dedykowane aplikacje Laravel i szczerze powiemy, gdy Twój projekt przerósł WordPress — złożona logika biznesowa, ciężkie integracje, procesy wielosystemowe. Jeśli WordPress pasuje — zbudujemy go dobrze. Jeśli nie — powiemy wprost.

WordPress zrobiony porządnie

Dedykowana funkcjonalność trafia do wtyczki lub hooków motywu — nigdy do bloba page-buildera:

add_action('rest_api_init', function () {
    register_rest_route('studio/v1', '/portfolio', [
        'methods'  => 'GET',
        'callback' => fn() => get_posts([
            'post_type'   => 'portfolio',
            'numberposts' => 12,
        ]),
        'permission_callback' => '__return_true',
    ]);
});

I anatomia zdrowej instalacji WordPress:

Browser ──► Nginx ──► PHP-FPM ──► WordPress
                              ├─► theme (custom, no builder)
                              ├─► plugins (minimal, maintained)
                              └─► MySQL ──► object cache (Redis)

Custom CRM and CMS Development for Your Highest Goals

Businesses require agile and effective automation means to operate successfully. CMS aka Content Management System and CRM aka Customer Relationship Management are among the most in-demand among them. They boost performance and help to control each process simultaneously. 

These two types of software are featured in multiple benefits:

  • Analysis of customers' behavior and sales rates.

Both of these systems can work separately or create a synergized system which will help to create impactful content and measure its impact on customers.  

The Most Significant Benefits of Our CMS/CRM Development Services

When you decide that you need CRM/CMS web development services, it can be a die-hard choice of whom to apply for them. In our company, we have a huge experience in how to build a CMS or CRM and how to make them work efficiently. We adhere to a couple of principles which make our CMS development service the best in the niche.

  • Individual approach to each project. We understand that each business is unique and thus, it requires custom solutions which encounter all the peculiarities.
  • Strict adherence to client’s requirements and needs. We investigate your needs in advance and follow them as a road map.

With our CRM system development company, you can get top-notch automation tools for your business.

 

How a custom CMS is structured

Our own CMS — the one running this site — is a Laravel app with a Filament admin panel, localized content model and AI tools wired in. The content flow looks like this:

Editor ──► Filament admin ──► pages / widgets / services (translations: en/uk/pl)

Розробка власних CRM і CMS для ваших найамбітніших цілей

Найважливіші переваги наших послуг з розробки CMS/CRM

Jak zbudowany jest dedykowany CMS

Nasz autorski CMS — ten, na którym działa ta strona — to aplikacja Laravel z panelem Filament, zlokalizowanym modelem treści i podpiętymi narzędziami AI. Przepływ treści wygląda tak:

Każda encja — strona, widget, usługa, pozycja menu — niesie swoje tłumaczenia w jednej kolumnie JSON, więc dodanie lokalizacji nigdy nie wymaga migracji ani nowej tabeli. en.title: E-commerce Development
en.description:
We build e-commerce that fits the business instead of forcing the business into a platform. Sometimes that's a properly set up WooCommerce store; sometimes it's a custom Laravel application when the catalogue, pricing rules or integrations get too specific for off-the-shelf solutions.

What we build

  • WooCommerce and WordPress-based stores for straightforward catalogues — fast to launch, easy to manage, cheap to run.
  • Custom e-commerce backends on Laravel — complex pricing, B2B flows, subscriptions, multi-warehouse stock, unusual product types.
  • Headless storefronts — a modern Vue/Nuxt frontend on top of an e-commerce or custom backend when page speed and UX are the competitive edge.
  • Marketplace and multi-vendor features — seller accounts, commission logic, payout flows.

The integrations that make a store work

A shop lives or dies by its plumbing: payment gateways (Stripe, PayPal, local providers), shipping and tax calculation, accounting and CRM sync, email flows, analytics. We've wired up payment processors, Zoho CRM, marketing automation and custom fulfillment systems — the store frontend is the easy part; making everything talk reliably is where experience counts.

How we approach a build

We start from your catalogue and order flow, not from a theme demo. What's the product structure? Who updates prices and stock? What happens on a failed payment? Once those answers are clear we pick the platform — and only then talk design. That order saves you from discovering at launch that your "simple" store needed custom development after all.

Bring us your product and your current setup — we'll sketch the shortest path to a store that works.

The order flow we build for

A checkout is a state machine, not a form. This is the flow we design around — every arrow is a place where money can be lost:

Cart ──► Checkout ──► Payment intent ──► Gateway (Stripe / PayPal)
            │                                    │
            │                              webhook ──► Order paid
            │                                    │
            └─► abandoned-cart email      failed ──► retry / support

That's why we insist on webhook-driven order state, idempotent payment handling and a queue for post-purchase work (invoices, emails, stock sync). A "place order" button that double-charges or silently loses orders isn't a UX problem — it's an architecture problem.

uk.title: Розробка e-commerce
uk.description:
Ми створюємо e-commerce, який підлаштовується під бізнес, а не змушує бізнес вкластись у платформу. Іноді це правильно налаштований магазин на WooCommerce; іноді — кастомний застосунок на Laravel, коли каталог, правила цін або інтеграції стають занадто специфічними для коробкових рішень.

Що ми створюємо

  • Магазини на WooCommerce і WordPress для прямолінійних каталогів — швидкий запуск, легке керування, дешева підтримка.
  • Кастомні e-commerce бекенди на Laravel — складні ціни, B2B-процеси, підписки, мультискладські залишки, нестандартні типи товарів.
  • Headless-вітрини — сучасний Vue/Nuxt фронтенд поверх e-commerce чи кастомного бекенда, коли швидкість сторінок і UX є конкурентною перевагою.
  • Маркетплейси й мультивендорні функції — акаунти продавців, логіка комісій, виплати.

Інтеграції, без яких магазин не працює

Магазин тримається на сантехніці: платіжні шлюзи (Stripe, PayPal, локальні провайдери), розрахунок доставки й податків, синхронізація з бухгалтерією та CRM, email-ланцюжки, аналітика. Ми підключали платіжні процесори, Zoho CRM, маркетингову автоматизацію та кастомні системи фулфілменту — фронтенд магазину це проста частина; змусити все надійно спілкуватись — ось де рахується досвід.

Як ми підходимо до розробки

Починаємо з вашого каталогу й потоку замовлень, а не з демки теми. Яка структура товарів? Хто оновлює ціни й залишки? Що відбувається при невдалій оплаті? Коли відповіді зрозумілі — обираємо платформу, і лише тоді говоримо про дизайн. Такий порядок рятує від відкриття на запуску, що вашому "простому" магазину все ж треба була кастомна розробка.

Приходьте з вашим продуктом і поточним сетапом — накидаємо найкоротший шлях до магазину, який працює.

Потік замовлення, під який ми будуємо

Чекаут — це state machine, а не форма. Це потік, навколо якого ми проєктуємо — кожна стрілка це місце, де можна втратити гроші:

Cart ──► Checkout ──► Payment intent ──► Gateway (Stripe / PayPal)
            │                                    │
            │                              webhook ──► Order paid
            │                                    │
            └─► abandoned-cart email      failed ──► retry / support

Тому ми наполягаємо на webhook-керованому стані замовлення, ідемпотентній обробці платежів і черзі для post-purchase роботи (інвойси, листи, синхронізація залишків). Кнопка "оформити замовлення", що двічі списує або мовчки губить замовлення — це не проблема UX, це проблема архітектури.

What we can build into your product

  • Content generation and translation pipelines — multi-step workflows that draft, review, translate and publish with human checkpoints where they matter. Our CMS (this site) has AI generation and translation built into the admin panel.
  • RAG and semantic search — embeddings, vector search and retrieval so an LLM answers from your data instead of hallucinating.

Pragmatic about providers

We're not married to one vendor. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, local models — we pick per task and budget, and we build with fallbacks so a provider outage or price hike doesn't take your feature down. Generation happens asynchronously with retries and audit records, so a flaky LLM doesn't mean a broken page.

Where AI doesn't belong

Just as important: we'll tell you when a rules engine or a simple script solves your problem better and cheaper than a model. A good AI integration is invisible — it saves someone an hour a day without anyone thinking about the model behind it.

How the pipeline works

NetPostPanel's generation pipeline — the same architecture we'd wire into your product:

Request ──► Prompt synthesis ──► LLM provider ──► Draft
                │                                     │
          RAG: embed ──► vector                 Semantic filter
          search ──► context                    (relevance check)
                                                      │

                                                      │
                                              Audit log + retry on failure

Every step is a discrete, testable unit — a prompt template, a retrieval call, a filter, a publish action — orchestrated asynchronously with retries. If the provider times out, the job retries; if the filter rejects the draft, it goes back for regeneration. Nothing reaches the public page unchecked.

en.title: API Integrations
en.description:
Every serious product ends up talking to other systems: payment gateways, CRMs, shipping providers, analytics, AI services, internal tools. We design and build those integrations so they survive real-world conditions — rate limits, timeouts, flaky third-party APIs and data that arrives in whatever shape the other side feels like sending.

Integrations we've shipped

  • CRM and sales — this site's contact forms push leads straight into Zoho CRM with proper error handling, so a Zoho hiccup never loses an inquiry.
  • Payments — Stripe and other gateways: checkout, subscriptions, webhooks, reconciliation.
  • AI providers — NetPostPanel orchestrates multiple LLM APIs behind a single internal interface with retries and fallbacks.
  • REST and GraphQL APIs — we both consume external APIs and build documented endpoints for your partners and mobile apps to consume.
  • Webhooks and event flows — inbound and outbound, with signature verification, queues and replay-safe processing.

Built to fail gracefully

The difference between an integration that works in a demo and one that works in production is failure handling. We build integrations with queues instead of synchronous calls where it matters, retries with backoff, idempotent processing, dead-letter visibility and audit trails — so when a third party is down at 3 AM, your users don't notice and nothing is silently lost.

Documentation that stays true

Integrations we build come with the mapping documented — which fields go where, what happens on each failure mode, how to rotate credentials. The next developer (maybe you, maybe us in two years) shouldn't have to reverse-engineer the plumbing.

If your systems live in silos and people copy data between them by hand — that's fixable. Tell us what should be talking to what.

What a solid integration looks like

Inbound webhook handling, the way we wire it — verify, queue, acknowledge fast:

public function handle(Request $request): JsonResponse
{
    abort_unless(
        hash_equals($expected, $request->header('X-Signature')),
        401
    );

    ProcessWebhook::dispatch($request->all())->onQueue('webhooks');

    return response()->json(['status' => 'accepted'], 202);
}

The full picture — synchronous where the user waits, queued where the work happens:

Third party ──► webhook ──► verify signature ──► queue ──► process ──► done
                                  │                     │
                                  └─► invalid ──► 401   └─► failed ──► retry → dead-letter

Most of our maintenance clients come to us with sites built by someone else — freelancers who moved on, agencies that closed, or code nobody has touched in three years. Maintenance isn't a retainer for unlimited work — we'll be upfront about what's covered and what counts as a project. But it does mean your site has an owner again: someone who knows where things are, updates them on schedule, and answers when something's wrong.

The maintenance loop

Maintenance is a loop, not a ticket queue. This is the routine running on the sites we look after:

Monitor (uptime, errors, slow queries)

    │                                                        │
    └────────────── weekly: updates, backups, report ◄────────┘

And the boring-but-critical pieces behind it: automated off-site backups with scheduled restore tests, dependency updates applied on a staging copy first, uptime and error tracking wired to alerts, and a written runbook so incidents don't depend on one person's memory.

en.title: Legacy Code Refactoring
en.description:
Inherited a codebase nobody wants to touch? We audit legacy PHP applications, map the risks, and refactor incrementally — without stopping your business or rewriting from scratch.

Typical work: framework upgrades, decoupling tangled code, adding tests to critical paths, fixing security issues and replacing abandoned dependencies. We modernize in small, safe steps that keep production stable.

Times do not stand still, and even the most effective website with time can become outdated. This concerns not only its content but technologies too. That’s why we offer businesses whose websites’ codes are outdated our help with legacy code refactoring.   

What’s the Essence of Legacy Code Refactoring Services

The main idea to refactor legacy code is to update its structure and architecture. That doesn’t impact the functionality of the code, but it helps to improve outdated code and, sometimes, to integrate outdated software or websites with newer products used by businesses.   

The Main Benefits of the Modernization of Legacy Applications and Sites  

There are multiple benefits which are essential for legacy code refactoring.  

  • It is cost-saving. You reduce costs by implementing the modernization of legacy applications instead of rebuilding it from scratch or developing a new one instead of an existing one.
  • It is referred to implementing newer and better practices without quitting previous ones.
  • Improved protection. As usual, outdated sites and apps are prone to breakdowns and hacks. When the code is updated, it provides improved protection levels.
  • The ability to scale the product up and provide more innovations in the future. That is bingo for growing businesses which have goals for further scaling up.
  • Easier integration with other products. When the code is outdated, and it has low interoperability, it’s a catastrophe. Legacy code refactoring helps to cope with this problem.

In DigiSpace, we focus on refactoring PHP legacy code by using new-gen frameworks. You can get Laravel upgrades or Symfony upgrades in our company. We can improve your website, app, or product performance for low costs. With us, you can update the PHP version of your web tool and get its highest performance ever. 

The strangler approach

We don't rewrite from scratch — we wrap the legacy system and replace it piece by piece:

        ┌─────────────┐         ┌──────────────┐
Users ──►  Legacy app  │         │  New module   │
        │  (shrinking) │ ──route─►  (Laravel)     │
        └──────┬──────┘         └──────┬───────┘
               │                       │
               └────── shared DB ◄─────┘

  Phase 1: route new features to new code
  Phase 2: migrate hot paths module by module
  Phase 3: legacy shrinks to nothing — retire it

Each migrated piece gets tests first — characterization tests that capture what the old code actually does, bugs included. Only then do we refactor. That's the difference between a migration and a gamble.

Навіть найскладніший вебсайт потребує надійного хостингу, щоб працювати бездоганно. Чи знали ви, що 70% вебсайтів у світі розміщені на серверах Ubuntu? З моменту свого створення в 1992 році ОС Linux і зокрема Ubuntu була визнана хостом №1 для вебсайтів. Це справді так з таких причин:

  • Висока надійність,
  • Виняткова стабільність роботи,
  • Висока продуктивність і ефективність.

Все це робить сервери Ubuntu найкращим вибором для вебсайтів, особливо в бізнес-сегменті.  

Декілька фактів на користь вибору серверів Ubuntu для хостингу вашого вебсайту

  • Кількість серверів на Linux удвічі перевищує кількість серверів на базі Windows.
  • Усі великі гравці у сфері вебхостингу працюють із серверами Ubuntu для надання послуг вебхостингу.
  • Ubuntu економічно вигідна завдяки своїй відкритій природі, але при цьому надійна й ефективна.

Як виглядає деплой

Наші деплої навмисно нудні — пайплайн цього сайту (GitHub Actions → реліз → атомарна заміна symlink) це той самий патерн, що ми налаштовуємо клієнтам:

push ──► CI: build + test suite ──► upload tarball
                                          │

                                          │
                              .env + storage shared ──► migrate --force ──► health check

А на сервері: Nginx + PHP-FPM, окремі версії PHP під сайт, Let's Encrypt TLS з автооновленням, fail2ban, файрвол, logrotate, крон під моніторингом. Релізи зберігаються, тож відкат — це один symlink, а не панічна SSH-сесія.

    location / {

    }
    location ~ \.php$ {
        fastcgi_pass unix:/run/php/php8.3-fpm.sock;
        include fastcgi_params;

}

Wdrożenia automatyzujemy gdzie to możliwe — pipeline'y CI/CD, wydania bez przestojów, rollbacki i monitoring. Nasza własna produkcja działa na dokładnie takiej konfiguracji.

Nawet najbardziej zaawansowana strona internetowa wymaga niezawodnego hostingu, aby działać bez zarzutu. Czy wiesz, że 70% stron na świecie jest hostowanych na serwerach Ubuntu? Kilka faktów przemawiających za wyborem serwerów Ubuntu do hostingu Twojej strony

  • Liczba serwerów Linux jest dwukrotnie wyższa niż liczba serwerów opartych na Windows.

  • Ubuntu jest ekonomiczna dzięki swojej otwartej naturze, a jednocześnie niezawodna i skuteczna.
  • Serwery Ubuntu idealnie współpracują z wieloma ekosystemami, w tym Perl, MySQL, Python, PHP i Ruby.
